s: Hi Phil.
您好，菲尔。
Georgie
Hi Georgie.
您好，乔治。
Phil
Georgie, how do you find tests and exams?
乔治，你怎么发现测试和考试？
Well, it's been a while since I've taken an exam, but when I was at school I was a bit of a nerd, so I actually quite enjoyed exams.
好吧，我从来没有参加过考试，但当我在学校时，我是一个疯子，所以我真的很喜欢考试。
Georgie
You know what?
你知道的吗？
Phil
Me too.
我也是。
But let's talk about Gen Z. Something is going on with Gen Z's test scores.
但让我们谈谈Z代。有什么正在发生在Z代的测试成绩。
Since 2012, when this generation were at school, results of a big international test of 15-year-olds have got worse.
自2012年以来，这个世代在学校学习以来，15岁儿童的大型国际测试结果变得更糟。
Today on 6 Minute English, we'll be hearing about some reasons why test scores are falling and asking, 'Is Gen Z getting less intelligent?'
今天在6分钟英语节目上，我们会听到一些测试成绩下降的原因，"Z代越来越不聪明吗？"
Well, speaking of tests, we'll start with our quiz question.
谈论测试，我们要从测试问题开始。
We're looking at some data from the Programme for International Students Assessment, or PISA, but how many 15-year-olds around the world take this assessment?
我们正在研究国际学生评估计划的一些数据，世界上有多少15岁的孩子接受这个评估？。
Phil, I'm not feeling too confident about this one.
菲尔，我对此不太自信。
Georgie
I might fail.
我可能会失败。
I'm going to go with b) 500,000.
我会选择b) 500万。
Well, we'll find out at the end of the programme.
我们将在节目结束时发现。
Phil
OK Phil.
好了，菲尔。
Georgie
So, you said that Gen Z's test scores have been falling.
所以，你说Z代的测试成绩一直在下降。
Can you explain a bit more?
你能解释更多吗？
OK.
没有问题。
Phil
So, every three years, 15-year-olds around the world take tests in reading, maths and science.
每三年，世界各地的15岁儿童都会参加阅读，数学和科学测试。
And the PISA tests started 25 years ago.
而PISA测试25年前才开始。
And if you look at the average scores across the 30 countries that have been doing it since the beginning, they're all going down.
如果你看看30个从一开始就这样做的国家的平均分数，它们都会下降。
OK.
没有问题。
Georgie
So, what is going on?
那么，发生了什么事？
Why are the test scores going down?
为什么测试成绩下降？
Well, the reasons behind the scores are complicated, but one factor that many experts point to is Covid.
结果背后的原因很复杂，但许多专家指出的一个因素是Covid。
Phil
Professor Amy Orben from the University of Cambridge explained more to the BBC World Service.
剑桥大学的艾米·奥尔本教授对BBC世界服务提供了更多的解释。
Covid was a massive disruption in our children's lives, with school closures as well as, just, disruptions in both the family and society.
科维德对我们的孩子们的生活造成了巨大破坏，学校关闭以及家庭和社会的破坏。
Amy Orben
Amy reminds us that Covid was a big disruption for school children.
艾米提醒我们，
Georgie
A disruption is something which stops someone from doing what they normally do.
干扰是阻止一个人做他们通常做的事情。
OK.
没有问题。
So, Covid has likely impacted test scores, but you mentioned that the scores have been lower since 2012, several years before Covid.
因此，Covid可能影响了测试成绩，但您提到，自2012年以来，在Covid之前的几年。
So, are there any other reasons for the fall in test scores?
所以，测试成绩下降还有其他原因吗？
Well, there's been another big change impacting schoolchildren in that time, and that's the use of technology.
另外一个重大变化影响了学校的学生，这就是技术的使用。
Phil
The theory is that replacing textbooks and notebooks with laptops and tablets in schools... it can directly affect test scores.
理论是，取代教科书，和笔记本电脑的笔记本，在学校的平板电脑... 它可以直接影响测试成绩。
Andreas Schleicher is the head of the PISA study, and he thinks we may be seeing the impact of tech in the test results.
艾德里亚斯·施莱赫 (Andreas Schleicher) 是PISA研究负责人，他认为我们可能会看到技术在测试结果的影响。
The elephant in the room is technology itself.
在房间里的象是技术本身。
Andreas Schleicher
If we were to see the same decline in all subject areas, you might say, "Well, education is deteriorating ," but that's not the case.
如果我们看到所有学科都出现了相同的下降，你可能会说"，教育正在恶化"，但情况并非如此。
The steep drop really is in reading, and this steep drop is along those lines that actually, you know, mark the digital world.
落的确是在阅读中，而落的确沿着那些线路，你知道的，标志着数字世界。
Andreas calls technology the elephant in the room , meaning the obvious thing that people don't want to talk about.
安德烈斯称技术是房间中的象，这意味着人们不想谈论的显而易见的事情。
Georgie
Right.
很好。
Phil
Andreas says that it's not true that all education is deteriorating , or getting worse.
安德烈斯说，所有教育都在恶化，或者变得更糟。
Andreas says there has been a steep drop , which means a big fall, in reading test scores in particular.
安德烈斯说有的跌幅，这意味着大跌倒，特别是在阅读测试成绩时。
Georgie
And he believes this suggests that learning through screens could be behind the scores.
他认为，这表明通过屏幕学习可能会落后。
So, Phil, do experts believe that we should stop using technology in schools?
所以，菲尔，专家认为我们应该停止在学校使用技术吗？
Well, it's complicated.
这很复杂。
Phil
Other evidence suggests that screens aren't the problem.
其他证据表明，屏幕并不是问题。
If we look at Singapore, students there have some of the best test scores in all subjects, but they also say they use technology in class more than almost anyone else.
如果我们看看新加坡，学生在所有科目中取得最好的成绩，但他们也说他们在课堂上使用技术比其他任何人都多。
And of course, 15-year-olds don't just use technology in schools.
当然，15岁的孩子不仅仅在学校使用技术。
Let's hear from Jade Bowler, an education content creator.
让我们听从Jade Bowler，一个教育内容创作者。
Even if you were to just put a blanket ban on technology at schools, they will come home to environments where they can go on their phone for as long as they like, if they want to.
即使你在学校全面禁止技术，他们会回家，可以使用手机的环境，如果他们愿意。
Jade Bowler
You know, they could literally come home after a day of not using tech and scroll for the next eight hours if they wanted to.
他们可以在一天不使用技术后回家，然后在接下来的八小时里滚动，如果他们愿意。
Jade talks about what might happen if there was a blanket ban on technology in schools.
杰德谈到如果学校全面禁止技术会发生什么。
Georgie
A blanket ban is completely stopping people from doing something.
一个全面的禁令完全阻止人们做某事。
Yes, and Jade points out that if technology in schools was banned, teenagers could scroll outside school, meaning they could look at the internet with no limits or end.
是的，杰德指出如果学校禁止技术，青少年可以在学校外滚动，这意味着他们可以看互联网，没有任何限制或终点。
Phil
So, are Gen Z getting less intelligent?
那么，Z一代变得不太聪明了吗？
Well, their PISA test scores have got worse, but as we've heard, their education has been impacted by some big changes.
他们的PISA测试成绩变得更糟，但我们听说，他们的教育受到一些重大变化的影响。
OK.
没有问题。
Georgie
Phil, I think it's time we revealed whether I have failed this week's quiz question.
菲尔，我认为是时候揭示我是否失败了本周的试题。
Well, yes.
是的，是的。
Phil
I asked you how many people take the PISA assessment and you said it was b) 500,000, which means you failed because it's c) 750,000.
我问你有多少人接受PISA评估，你说是b) 500万，这意味着你失败了，因为c) 75万。
OK.
没有问题。
Georgie
It's time to recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with disruption , which means stopping people doing what they normally do.
现在是时候重新总结了我们在这个节目中学到的词汇，从干扰开始，这意味着停止人们做他们通常做的事情。
The expression the elephant in the room is used to refer to something that's obvious, but nobody is talking about.
象在房间中的表达式是指明显的东西，但没有人谈论。
Phil
If something deteriorates , it gets worse.
如果事情恶化，它会变得更糟。
Georgie
A steep drop is a big fall.
一个落就是一个大跌落。
Phil
A blanket ban means completely stopping someone from doing something.
一个全面的禁令意味着完全阻止某人做某事。
Georgie
And if someone scrolls , they look at the internet with no limits or end.
如果有人滚动，他们会看互联网，没有任何限制或终点。
Phil
Once again, our six minutes are up.
再一次，我们的六分钟已经过去了。
Georgie
Thanks for joining us and goodbye.
谢谢你加入我们，再见。
Phil
Goodbye!
见面！
Georgie

w.deteriorates: v. 恶化，变坏( deteriorate的第三人称单数 )
w.scroll: n. 卷轴，画卷，名册；v. (使)成卷形
w.scrolls: n. （常用于录写正式文件的）纸卷( scroll的名词复数 )，卷轴，涡卷形（装饰）；v. （电脑屏幕上）从上到下移动
w.recap: vt. 翻新胎面；n. 翻新的轮胎
